prodSQL:
select 'constraint' as kind,
       lower(rel.relname || '.' || con.conname) as identifier
from pg_constraint con
join pg_class rel on rel.oid = con.conrelid
join pg_namespace nsp on nsp.oid = rel.relnamespace
where nsp.nspname = 'public'
  and con.conrelid <> 0            -- exclude domain/other constraints (table constraints only)
  and con.contype in ('c','f','u','p','x')  -- check, foreign key, unique, primary key, exclusion
order by identifier;
norm: Lowercased `table.constraint_name`. Extraction: table = the bare last segment captured by RE_ALTER (optional `public.`/other schema qualifier and double-quotes stripped), constraint = the identifier after ADD CONSTRAINT (quotes stripped); joined `table + '.' + name`, lowercased. Prod: lower(pg_class.relname || '.' || pg_constraint.conname) for public-schema table constraints. Postgres constraint names are unique per table (a table cannot hold two constraints of the same name), so (table, conname) is an exact, collision-free key regardless of constraint type â€” the type is intentionally NOT part of the identifier. All real identifiers in the repo are unquoted lowercase, so lowercasing both sides is loss-free here.
regexes: STRIP FIRST (order matters): block comments /\/\*[\s\S]*?\*\//g then line comments /--[^\n]*/g
RE_ALTER (table, with offsets via matchAll; g+i): /\balter\s+table\s+(?:if\s+exists\s+)?(?:only\s+)?(?:"?[a-zA-Z_][a-zA-Z0-9_$]*"?\s*\.\s*)?"?([a-zA-Z_][a-zA-Z0-9_$]*)"?/gi
RE_DROP (constraint name, for net-state subtraction; g+i): /\bdrop\s+constraint\s+(?:if\s+exists\s+)?"?([a-zA-Z_][a-zA-Z0-9_$]*)"?/gi

PAIRING (not a regex): for each RE_ADD/RE_DROP match at index i, governing table = table of the ALTER match with the greatest index < i AND sql.slice(alterIndex, i).indexOf(';') === -1; else orphan -> discard. Emit `${table.toLowerCase()}.${name.toLowerCase()}`.
fpFilters: Comments stripped before scanning (-- line and /* */ block), so commented-out DDL is never counted.

Orphan ADD/DROP CONSTRAINT (no governing ALTER TABLE in the same statement â€” none preceding, or a ';' between) is discarded. This structurally drops phantoms from Gherkin/prose and dynamic-SQL text living inside $$...$$ bodies, since such text lacks a real `ALTER TABLE <ident> ... ADD CONSTRAINT` with no intervening ';'.
Drop any identifier whose TABLE part === 'public' â€” the classic phantom where a schema name is mis-captured as a table (mirrors the fake `public` table the tables gate guards against).
Drop identifiers whose table or name is a bare SQL keyword accidentally captured from prose (e.g. table/constraint/exists/not/if) â€” belt-and-suspenders.

Reviewed allowlist file scripts/ci/db-constraints-allowlist.json (shape {"constraints": ["table.name", ...]}) for constraints intentionally dropped/renamed out of band, or confirmed phantoms from a future function body / dynamic SQL. Keep it shrinking; a false positive is cheap (allowlist it) but a false negative is not.
Zero-scan tripwire: an empty final set fails closed rather than passing vacuously.
fixes: Close the predicate-drift gap for the redefined constraints: have the prod SQL also return pg_get_constraintdef(con.oid) as condef, capture the net-final constraint BODY from the migration text (everything after the name up to the statement terminator), normalize both (collapse whitespace, lowercase keywords, canonicalize IN(...) vs = ANY(ARRAY[...])), and diff. At minimum gate the CHECK (contype='c') and FK (contype='f') bodies for names that are DROP+re-ADD'd more than once - that is the exact set (email_send_log_status_check, agent_fix_queue_status_check, classes checks) where a stale predicate is known to be the risk.

Before computing offsets and the semicolon-between scan, mask (replace with equal-length spaces) single-quoted string literals, dollar-quoted spans ($$...$$, $tag$...$tag$, $g$...$g$, $cron$...$cron$), in addition to the comments already stripped. This keeps a ';' inside a CHECK body or Gherkin/DO text from corrupting statement boundaries, and hardens the primary orphan/phantom defense against future compound multi-ADD statements. Keep the ADD/DROP CONSTRAINT keyword matching on the masked text but recover the actual name from the original offsets.

Strengthen the tripwire from `size===0` to a floor: assert the final declared count is >= a committed baseline (today ~20) or fail closed, so a partial capture regression is caught, not just total wipeout. Store the baseline next to the allowlist and require it to move deliberately.

Explicitly confirm (in the spec and in CI) that inline CREATE TABLE / column-level constraints are owned by a separate present-check category and that class_module_progress_pkey, class_module_sections title/summary CHECKs, etc. are actually verified there; otherwise this category's scope-out becomes an unowned blind spot for the never-applied-inline case.

prodSQL:
select 'column' as kind,
       c.relname || '.' || a.attname as identifier
from pg_catalog.pg_attribute a
join pg_catalog.pg_class      c on c.oid = a.attrelid
join pg_catalog.pg_namespace  n on n.oid = c.relnamespace
where n.nspname = 'public'
  and c.relkind in ('r','p')      -- ordinary + partitioned base tables (declared columns live on tables)
  and a.attnum > 0                -- exclude system columns (ctid, oid, ...)
  and not a.attisdropped          -- exclude columns dropped in prod (a dropped col is genuine drift vs a declaration)
order by 1,2;
-- Returns lowercase relname.attname for unquoted identifiers, matching the extractor's normalization exactly.
-- Restricted to relkind r/p (not views/matviews) on purpose: a view column must never mask a missing table
-- column (that would hide drift = false negative). This makes the gate stricter, i.e. fail-closed.
-- (If the fetch harness expects the column alias 'name' as in check-db-objects-present.mjs, alias identifier AS name.)
norm: Lowercased "table.column": strip any leading schema qualifier (public.) and surrounding double-quotes from BOTH the table and the column, join with a single dot, lowercase the whole string. Examples: `ALTER TABLE public.profiles ADD COLUMN portfolio_url ...` -> `profiles.portfolio_url`; inside `CREATE TABLE public.email_send_log ( ... recipient_email TEXT ... )` -> `email_send_log.recipient_email`. Prod side produces the identical form via `relname || '.' || attname` (already lowercase for unquoted identifiers). Assumes all identifiers are unquoted/lowercase (true across the corpus); a mixed-case quoted identifier would need case-preserving comparison and is listed as a known gap.
regexes: SANITIZE line comments: /--[^\n]*/g  ->  ' '  (apply only within the single-pass lexer, not standalone)
SANITIZE single-quoted strings incl. E'' and doubled '': /(?:[eE])?'(?:\\.|''|[^'])*'/g  ->  "''"
DOLLAR-QUOTE tag finder (then match identical tag; KEEP span iff preceding token matches /\bDO\s*$/i, else STRIP): /\$([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*)?\$/g

CREATE TABLE header locator (capture table, then paren-match the body starting at the '('; note the required '(' and identifier make public.%I unmatchable): /\bcreate\s+table\s+(?:if\s+not\s+exists\s+)?(?:"?public"?\s*\.\s*)?"?([a-z_][a-z0-9_$]*)"?\s*\(/gi
CREATE TABLE body: split on depth-1 commas via a paren-depth counter (NOT regex), then per item skip-if-constraint: /^\s*(?:constraint|primary|foreign|unique|check|exclude|like|references|key)\b/i
CREATE TABLE body: first-column-identifier extractor per surviving item: /^\s*"?([a-z_][a-z0-9_$]*)"?/i
fpFilters: Any identifier whose table part OR column part contains a character outside [a-z0-9_$] after unquoting -- primarily the '%' from dynamic `format('CREATE TABLE public.%I ...')` / `format('... ALTER TABLE %I ADD COLUMN ...')` in reference_* loops (20260502180318, 20260502184658, and the ~25 %I files). Belt-and-suspenders: the CREATE/ALTER regexes already fail to match %I, so these mostly never enter the set.

The bare schema token `public` as a table name (the classic 'fake table named public' phantom): the CREATE TABLE regex captures the identifier AFTER an optional public. prefix and never `public` itself, so `public.<t>` yields `<t>`; reject any emitted table literally equal to `public`.

Constraint keywords mis-read as column names in a CREATE TABLE body (constraint|primary|foreign|unique|check|exclude|like|references|key) -- excluded by the constraint-skip regex; filter again as a guard.

Renamed-away columns general_applications.servant_leadership_definition / servant_leadership_actions / servant_leadership_challenges / servant_leadership_situation (renamed to service_leadership_* in 20260522031707) -- handled by RENAME subtraction; if RENAME handling is disabled these four must be allowlisted.

Anything recovered from stripped regions: CREATE FUNCTION/PROCEDURE/TRIGGER `AS $$...$$` bodies and single-quoted string literals (Gherkin/prose in bdd_scenarios, known_issue_catalog, security *_scenarios INSERT...VALUES) -- removed in STEP 1, so they cannot reach the set.

Columns on non-public tables (e.g. a future ADD COLUMN on realtime.messages) -- the public-only prod query would report them absent; allowlist rather than let them fail spuriously (still fail-closed, never silently passed).
fixes: Fix the constraint-skip keyword list to the exact set of Postgres table-constraint / table-element leading keywords: CONSTRAINT | PRIMARY | FOREIGN | UNIQUE | CHECK | EXCLUDE | LIKE. REMOVE `key` and `references` â€” neither can begin a table-level constraint (KEY only ever follows PRIMARY/FOREIGN; REFERENCES is a column-level constraint clause, never the first token of a table element). This immediately recovers feature_flags.key, support_categories.key and the other 4. Add a regression assertion that `key text PRIMARY KEY` yields column `key`.

Harden the ALTER TABLE and CREATE TABLE header regexes to consume an ARBITRARY schema prefix `(?:"?([a-z_][a-z0-9_$]*)"?\s*\.\s*)?` and capture it; when the captured schema is present and not `public`, route the column to the non-public allowlist path (or skip) rather than letting the schema token be captured as the table name. Prevents the `realtime.<col>` misattribution.

Keep the DO-block classifier but broaden the keep-test to tolerate `DO [LANGUAGE <lang>] $tag$` (skip an optional LANGUAGE clause between DO and the opening tag) so a labelled DO block with ADD COLUMN is never misread as a stripped function body.

Retain the zero-scan tripwire and additionally assert a sane floor (e.g. derived columns >> number of declared tables) so a future regex regression that silently halves the set is caught, not just the all-zero case.

prodSQL:
SELECT 'cron_job'::text AS kind, jobname AS identifier
FROM cron.job
WHERE jobname IS NOT NULL;
-- FAIL CLOSED: pg_cron lives in schema `cron`. If the extension was never enabled
-- on this project, `cron.job` does not exist and this statement raises
-- "relation cron.job does not exist" (HTTP 400/500 from the Management API SQL
-- endpoint) â€” the gate MUST treat that as failure, never as "zero jobs, all good."
-- That silent skip is precisely the original outage (jobs existed only on the old
-- Lovable project; pg_cron was never enabled on pzvqxdgoztbfikfuifix). Do NOT wrap
-- in to_regclass()/EXISTS guards that would let absence pass. jobname is unique per
-- role in pg_cron >=1.4 (Supabase); returns one row per live scheduled job.
norm: Identifier = the cron job name: the first argument literal of cron.schedule(...), with its surrounding single-quote (or, defensively, double-quote / $tag$...$tag$) delimiters removed and outer whitespace trimmed. Compare EXACTLY and CASE-SENSITIVELY against cron.job.jobname. pg_cron stores jobname verbatim (it is a text value, not an SQL identifier), so names such as 'auth_email_watchdog_15m' and 'edge-deploy-smoke-10min' must match byte-for-byte â€” do NOT lowercase either side (unlike the table/function derivation, which lowercases unquoted identifiers). Treat the name as an opaque string that may contain hyphens, underscores, and digits.
fpFilters: Any cron.schedule/cron.unschedule text inside a -- line comment or /* */ block comment (stripped BEFORE matching) â€” e.g. 20260316051305:257 `-- ... cron.unschedule('process-email-queue')`, 20260707200000:25 `-- original cron.schedule(...) call`, 20260708170000:4 `-- cron.schedule() in a migration...`, 20260809120010:4 `-- Root cause: cron.schedule('reconcile-stuck-emails', â€¦)`

The prose token `cron.schedule(...)` / `cron.schedule()` with an ellipsis or empty parens â€” the extractor requires a quoted literal immediately after `(`, so these never capture a name; listed for completeness

Defensive: drop any captured first-arg that is actually a cron SCHEDULE expression or interval rather than a name â€” matches /^[\d*\/,\-\s]+$/ (e.g. '* * * * *', '*/5 * * * *', '0 3 * * *') or /^\d+\s+seconds?$/ (e.g. '5 seconds', '30 seconds'). These are 2nd args and are never captured by the 3-arg extractor, but this guards against a future 2-arg cron.schedule(schedule, command) form being mistaken for a named job

unschedule-only names that are NOT scheduled (correctly excluded because they never follow cron.schedule() â€” e.g. the short aliases 'prewarm-ugc-worker-30s' and 'process-freescout-events-15s' appear only inside cron.unschedule(... jobname IN (...)) cleanup lists)

Renamed/superseded/decommissioned jobs that legitimately no longer exist in prod (e.g. 'drain-notification-outbox' superseded by 'drain-notification-fanout-jobs') â†’ not code phantoms but expected over-extraction; retire via the reviewed allowlist with a reason, never by loosening the extractor
fixes: Add a reconciliation tripwire that makes the dynamic-name/2-arg false negative STRUCTURALLY impossible: after comment-stripping, count occurrences of /cron\.schedule\s*\(/gi and assert it EQUALS the number of captured names; on any inequality FAIL CLOSED ('a cron.schedule call site produced no literal job name'). Verified 66==66 today, so it passes now and trips the instant a non-literal/auto-named form is introduced. This is the single most important addition â€” the current zero-scan-only tripwire cannot catch a single dropped job.

Ship the reviewed allowlist NOW with at least the two decommissioned jobs and reasons: drain-notification-outbox (superseded by drain-notification-fanout-jobs, unscheduled 20260427041239) and triage-digest-daily (removed by 20260822160000_remove_triage_digest.sql). Without it the gate produces 2 false positives on correct prod on day one.
Wire the recommended 'reject non-literal first arg to cron.schedule' lint into the gate itself rather than leaving it as prose in knownGaps â€” a rule only documented is not enforced.

Fix the consumer/column contract: the SQL returns kind='cron_job', identifier=jobname, but the existing script reads r.name / kind in {table,function}. Either alias the SQL column to `name` and add a prodJobs branch on kind='cron_job', or write a dedicated consumer that reads r.identifier. Otherwise cron rows silently map to undefined (fail-closed but a wrong/confusing signal).

Resolve the normalization contradiction: compare jobname VERBATIM (no whitespace trim) and case-sensitively, so it matches pg_cron's byte-for-byte text storage; drop the 'outer whitespace trimmed' clause.

Confirm the fail-closed-on-missing-cron.job path is wired as an ERROR propagation: if the cron branch is UNION ALL'd into the main PROD_QUERY, a non-existent cron.job errors the whole query -> res not ok -> existing gate already fails closed (good); if run as a separate query, ensure the same non-2xx handling. The spec's intent here is correct and is the key win â€” just verify the integration keeps it.

prodSQL:
-- Read-only. Returns every base/partitioned table with RLS turned ON, in any
-- user-visible schema, normalized to lower(schema).lower(table) to match extraction.
-- Extra rows never cause false negatives (gate asserts declared IS-SUBSET-OF this set).
select
  'rls_enabled' as kind,
  lower(n.nspname) || '.' || lower(c.relname) as identifier
from pg_class c
join pg_namespace n on n.oid = c.relnamespace
where c.relkind in ('r','p')          -- ordinary + partitioned tables (RLS-capable)
  and c.relrowsecurity = true          -- RLS ENABLED (this category); NOT relforcerowsecurity
  and n.nspname not in ('pg_catalog','information_schema','pg_toast')
order by 1, 2;
norm: "lower(schema).lower(table)" â€” schema-qualified, dot-separated, all lowercased. Schema defaults to "public" when the ALTER omits it (none observed, but safe). Extraction lowercases the captured (schema, table); prod SQL emits lower(n.nspname)||'.'||lower(c.relname). Examples: public.invitations, public.feature_flags, realtime.messages, public.reference_skills.
regexes: DYNAMIC marker (file uses a templated %I enable loop): /\.\s*%i\s+enable\s+row\s+level\s+security/i
ARRAY block (recover dynamic table names, run only when marker matched): /array\s*\[([\s\S]*?)\]/gi
ARRAY element (harvest inside each block, add as public.<name>): /'([a-z_][a-z0-9_]*)'/gi
Comment strip applied BEFORE matching: /\/\*[\s\S]*?\*\//g -> ' ' then /--[^\n]*/g -> ' '
fpFilters: Any captured table containing '%' (e.g. %I / %i / %s / %L) â€” dollar-quoted format() template targets from EXECUTE loops, not real tables (both files 20260502180318 and 20260502184658 hit this; validated skipped).

The literal schema word captured AS a table (bare 'public','table','only','if','exists') cannot occur with the anchored ENABLE regex â€” validated 0 such captures across 711 files â€” but keep them on an ignore list if the regex is ever loosened.

Array-harvest over-extraction: when scoped to ARRAY[...] it is clean today, but any non-table string literal inside such an array in a future %I-loop file would be over-added â€” resolve via the reviewed db-objects allowlist, never by loosening the no-false-negative bias.

Supabase/platform-managed schemas surfaced by the broad prod query (realtime, storage, vault, graphql, extensions) â€” harmless: the gate only checks declared-subset-of-prod, so extra prod rows are ignored, never matched against.
fixes: Resolve the spec/harness contradiction in favor of the documented behavior: DELETE the DROP-subtraction entirely (rls_extract_test.mjs lines 71-73 and the RE_DROP definition). This restores the 213-table set, retains profiles and the other 8 publication-only 'drops', and eliminates the false-negative class. Then correct declaredCountApprox to 213 and re-run verification so the stated number matches the documented algorithm.

If any DROP subtraction is ever reintroduced, anchor RE_DROP to a statement boundary so it cannot match 'ALTER PUBLICATION ... DROP TABLE': require start-of-statement, e.g. match only after a ';' or start-of-string, /(^|;)\s*drop\s+table\b/ , and explicitly exclude lines containing 'alter publication'. Test it against 20260426221452 (profiles), 20260412202652 (notifications/project_applications), 20260513024219, 20260519172544, 20260531015413, 20260609132534 â€” none of those must reduce the enabled set.

Add an explicit non-regression assertion to the harness/gate: public.profiles MUST be in the declared RLS set (fail the derivation if not). A gate whose derivation can silently drop the primary PII table is not fail-closed.
Generalize the reused prod-row parser to handle kind==='rls_enabled' reading the 'identifier' column (the prod SQL emits identifier, not name); otherwise the reused shell ignores every rls row.

Keep the zero-scan tripwire but raise/Ã¦ttach a category-specific floor: e.g. fail if the rls_enabled declared set is unexpectedly small (well under ~200), so a future regression in the ENABLE/array logic can't quietly shrink the checked set to a vacuous pass.

Broaden the dynamic-loop marker beyond /.%i enable.../ (or detect any FOREACH ... IN ARRAY loop whose body contains 'enable row level security') so a future non-%I dynamic loader is not silently missed; until then, document that new dynamic RLS loaders must use the %I template or be added to a supplementary declared-list.

prodSQL: select 'table' as kind, c.relname as identifier from pg_catalog.pg_class c join pg_catalog.pg_namespace n on n.oid = c.relnamespace where n.nspname = 'public' and c.relkind in ('r','p') order by identifier;  -- relkind r = ordinary table, p = partitioned table; deliberately excludes views(v)/matviews(m)/foreign(f)/sequences(S). relname from an unquoted-created table is already lowercase; the gate lowercases both sides before diffing.
norm: Bare table name only (schema stripped â€” everything declared is in public and prod is queried only for public), unquoted, lowercased. e.g. declared `CREATE TABLE public.Feature_Flags` and prod relname `feature_flags` both normalize to the string "feature_flags". Compare declared-set vs prod-set as lowercased plain strings.
fpFilters: %I and any name containing '%' â€” dynamic format() placeholder, never a real table; route to the dynamic-sidecar tripwire instead of the set
the bare word 'public' captured as a name â€” happens if prose/DDL writes 'CREATE TABLE public' with no dot; public is a schema, never a table â€” hard-exclude

SQL keywords captured from Gherkin/prose inside dollar-quoted bodies (e.g. a bdd_scenarios INSERT or a Given/When/Then line containing 'create table ...') â€” over-extraction is safe (allowlist), but keep a small reserved-word denylist (public, table, if, not, exists) as a guard
reference_roles â€” created dynamically then dropped via `DROP TABLE IF EXISTS public.reference_roles CASCADE` (20260503180621); must NOT be in the dynamic sidecar's live set

tables that were created then legitimately dropped-and-not-recreated (passkey_credentials, passkey_login_sessions, passkey_recovery_tokens, passkey_login_challenges, career_plans, career_plan_items, accessibility_training_completions) â€” correctly excluded by the strict-drop subtraction; if any is intentionally still-present, allowlist rather than loosen the drop regex
fixes: Model ALTER TABLE ... RENAME TO in the same left-to-right event stream: on a rename, DELETE the old name and ADD the new name. Regex e.g. /alter\s+table\s+(?:if\s+exists\s+)?(?:"?public"?\s*\.\s*)?"?([a-z0-9_]+)"?\s+rename\s+to\s+"?([a-z0-9_]+)"?/gi , applied AFTER creates/drops in file order so reference_team_functions->reference_job_functions resolves correctly. This must apply to dynamically-derived names too (feed sidecar names into the same stream), not just statically-extracted ones.

Fix knownGap #1: it is factually wrong. State that exactly one table rename exists today (20260503180621: reference_team_functions -> reference_job_functions) and that the gate MUST model renames now, not 'before any rename migration lands'.

Correct the dynamic live set: remove reference_team_functions, add reference_job_functions (net still 18). Best implemented by the rename-in-stream fix above rather than editing the sidecar by hand, since reference_job_functions does not originate from a placeholder-CREATE file and cannot be keyed by one.

Add a fail-closed tripwire: if the migrations contain an ALTER TABLE ... RENAME TO but the rename model is absent/disabled, FAIL rather than silently under-verify â€” mirrors the %I placeholder tripwire.

Broaden the dynamic-DDL tripwire beyond '%': also trip on EXECUTE ... 'CREATE TABLE' with || concatenation or quote_ident so a future non-format() dynamic create cannot silently extract nothing. (No occurrences today, so this is preventive.)
Scope the comment stripper so /* */ removal does not cross dollar-quote boundaries (strip comments only outside $tag$...$tag$ spans), preventing an unbounded swallow of real DDL.

prodSQL:
select 'type' as kind, t.typname as identifier
from pg_type t
join pg_namespace n on n.oid = t.typnamespace
where n.nspname = 'public'
  and t.typname not like '\_%'
  and (
        t.typtype in ('e','r')
     or (t.typtype = 'c' and exists (
           select 1 from pg_class c where c.oid = t.typrelid and c.relkind = 'c'))
  )
union all
select 'enum_value' as kind, (t.typname || ':' || e.enumlabel) as identifier
from pg_enum e
join pg_type t on t.oid = e.enumtypid
join pg_namespace n on n.oid = t.typnamespace
where n.nspname = 'public';
norm: Dimension 1 (type existence): lowercased bare typname, schema prefix and surrounding double-quotes stripped (`public.cohort_status`, `"cohort_status"` -> `cohort_status`); matches pg_type.typname lowercased. Dimension 2 (enum labels): lowercased `typname:label` with SQL doubled single-quotes ('') collapsed to one '; matches `typname || ':' || enumlabel` lowercased. Both scoped to public schema.
fpFilters: public â€” schema token; never a type name. Exclude if ever captured (defensive; the regex captures the token after optional `public.`, so it cannot capture bare `public` from a well-formed statement, but the tables-category has a documented phantom-`public` risk).

membership_tier_old, cohort_status_old â€” created via ALTER TYPE RENAME (not CREATE) and immediately DROPped in the swap; never real prod objects. Never captured by the CREATE regex; exclude any `%_old` name defensively.
if, not, exists, or, replace â€” keywords; cannot be captured because the regex consumes `if not exists` explicitly, but listed as defensive allowlist entries.

Enum labels removed by the rename/swap recreate: cohort_status:open, cohort_status:live, cohort_status:completed, membership_tier:free, membership_tier:paid â€” declared in an earlier CREATE TYPE body but dropped by a later recreate. Source-order replay excludes them automatically; a naive all-ever-declared label check MUST allowlist them.

Any type/label name appearing only inside a $$...$$ prose/Gherkin/dynamic-SQL body (none today) â€” handled via the reviewed `types` allowlist in scripts/ci/db-objects-allowlist.json, since $$ bodies cannot be stripped without losing the 8 real DO-block CREATE TYPEs.

prodSQL:
-- Returns (kind, identifier) for every live view AND materialized view in the public schema.
-- pg_matviews is REQUIRED: materialized views do NOT appear in pg_views / information_schema.views.
-- pg_catalog views are used (not information_schema) to avoid privilege-based row filtering.
SELECT 'view'::text AS kind,
       'public.' || v.viewname AS identifier
FROM pg_catalog.pg_views v
WHERE v.schemaname = 'public'
UNION ALL
SELECT 'materialized_view'::text AS kind,
       'public.' || m.matviewname AS identifier
FROM pg_catalog.pg_matviews m
WHERE m.schemaname = 'public'
ORDER BY identifier;
norm: schema '.' name, with Postgres identifier folding applied so it matches pg_views.viewname / pg_matviews.matviewname exactly. Rules: schema defaults to 'public' when the migration omits it. Unquoted identifiers are lowercased (Postgres folds unquoted to lowercase). Double-quoted identifiers: strip the surrounding quotes, unescape doubled quotes ("" -> "), and preserve inner case verbatim (do NOT lowercase). Prod side already returns the raw stored name, so 'public.' || viewname matches. All current declarations are unquoted+lowercase, so every identifier is of the form public.<lowercase_name> (e.g. public.framework_search_mv). Reconciliation compares on identifier ONLY (case-sensitive after folding; a case-insensitive fallback compare is acceptable and stays fail-closed since it only ever ADMITS more matches for present names â€” but never use it to drop a name from the expected set). The 'kind' column is metadata, not part of the match key.
fpFilters: Line comments: '-- Recreate view with security_invoker = true' (20260415012656) is the exact 33rd substring hit; removed by the line-comment strip AND by \b (the 'create' inside 'reCREATE' has no word boundary).

Dollar-quoted bodies ($$...$$ and $tag$...$tag$): any 'CREATE VIEW'/'CREATE MATERIALIZED VIEW' appearing as PL/pgSQL body text or embedded Gherkin/BDD prose is stripped before matching, preventing phantom view objects (the same mechanism that would otherwise mint a fake table named 'public' for other categories).
Single-quoted seed/INSERT literals (e.g. bdd_scenarios Given/When/Then rows): stripped defensively; none currently contain 'create view', verified.
Schema token is never mistaken for the view name: the regex captures schema and name as separate groups, so 'CREATE VIEW public.x' yields name=x, never 'public'.

DROP statements are matched separately and only subtract from the expected set; a stray keyword after the name (WITH/AS/CASCADE) is never captured as an identifier because the name group terminates at whitespace/'.'/quote boundary.
fixes: Replace the four independent strip regexes with a single left-to-right SQL scanner that, at each position, consumes whichever of {line comment, block comment, single-quoted string, dollar-quoted string} opens FIRST, emitting only code text. Reordering the passes is insufficient because strings and dollar-quotes mutually nest; only a single-pass tokenizer is structurally sound. Apply CREATE/DROP matching to the code-only residue.

Add a fail-closed floor: commit an explicit expected-view manifest (the 19 distinct net-present identifiers) and FAIL the gate if the extracted Expected set does not equal it (or at minimum is smaller than it). This converts the vacuous/empty-set pass into a failure and makes an extraction regression loud.

Add a dedicated dynamic-DDL tripwire: scan the STRIPPED-OUT bodies for /EXECUTE[\s\S]{0,120}CREATE[\s\S]{0,40}VIEW/i and FAIL if found, so a future EXECUTE 'CREATE VIEW ...' cannot be silently ignored.

Fix declaredCountApprox to the distinct net-present count (19), or split into {createStatements:32, distinctExpectedPresent:19}, so the number is a usable cross-check against the reconciled Expected set.

Optional hardening: have the introspection SQL also emit each object's kind AND enforce kind against the declared kind (materialized vs plain) once existence is solid, closing the disclosed KIND-drift gap.

prodSQL:
select 'trigger' as kind, lower(n.nspname || '.' || c.relname || '.' || t.tgname) as identifier from pg_catalog.pg_trigger t join pg_catalog.pg_class c on c.oid = t.tgrelid join pg_catalog.pg_namespace n on n.oid = c.relnamespace where t.tgisinternal = false and n.nspname not in ('pg_catalog','information_schema') order by identifier;
-- kind is the literal 'trigger'. identifier is EXACTLY schema.table.triggername, lowercased, matching extraction output (which defaults omitted schema to 'public'). tgisinternal=false drops system/RI FK-enforcement triggers (which migrations never declare) but KEEPS user CONSTRAINT triggers. NOT restricted to schema='public' on purpose: real triggers target auth.users and pgmq.q_auth_emails / pgmq.q_transactional_emails, so a public-only filter would silently pass while an auth/pgmq trigger is unapplied. pg_trigger/pg_class/pg_namespace are world-readable catalogs, so the Management API role sees triggers in auth and pgmq regardless of table ownership. Returning extra prod rows (schemas we don't declare into) is harmless: the gate only checks declared âŠ† prod.
norm: "schema.table.triggername", all three segments lowercased and unquoted; schema defaults to 'public' when the CREATE/DROP ON clause omits it. Postgres trigger names are unique per-table (not global), and the same name recurs on different tables in this repo (e.g. trg_block_audit_mutation, trg_fw_kb_sync), so the table (with its schema) is a mandatory part of the key. Examples: public.profiles.update_profiles_updated_at ; auth.users.on_auth_user_created ; pgmq.q_auth_emails.trg_notify_email_worker_auth. Prod side builds the identical string via lower(n.nspname||'.'||c.relname||'.'||t.tgname).
fpFilters: Any identifier containing '%' (e.g. public.%i.trg_audit_%i_change, public.%i.trg_fw_kb_sync, public.%i.trg_ugc_translate_%i) â€” these come from EXECUTE format('CREATE TRIGGER ...%I... ON public.%I', ...) and are unresolvable statically; excluded from the verified set and reported as a known gap (NOT silently allowlisted).

Line/block comments stripped before matching so 'CREATE'/'trigger' inside comments does not count: '-- Recreate triggers under new names' (20260503180621:17), '-- Create trigger on projects table' (20260319225720:105), '-- Create the trigger if it doesn't exist' (20260315192526:27), and prose like '...trigger to also fire when status transitions...' (20260505002310:2).

Schema-name-as-table phantom (the 'fake public table' trap): prevented structurally â€” because '%' is inside the identifier char class, 'ON public.%I' matches schema='public', table='%i' (then %-filtered), instead of backtracking to table='public'. No allowlist entry needed.

Residual prose phantoms from $$...$$ bodies/Gherkin that happen to match the full CREATE TRIGGER <name> ... ON <x>.<y> shape: extremely unlikely given the required shape; any that occur surface as declared-but-absent FAILs (fail-closed) and get moved to a reviewed name+table allowlist with a reason, per the over-extraction bias.
fixes: Pull the dynamic-trigger mitigation INTO this spec rather than deferring it. Add a companion prod assertion per dynamic-loop function: SELECT count(*) FROM pg_trigger t JOIN pg_proc p ON p.oid=t.tgfoid JOIN pg_namespace n ON n.oid=p.pronamespace WHERE t.tgisinternal=false AND n.nspname='public' AND p.proname IN ('set_reference_updated_at','set_reference_search_tsv','audit_public_table_change','tg_sync_reference_to_kb','enqueue_ugc_translation_jobs', ...) GROUP BY p.proname; then FAIL if any expected fan-out function has 0 (loop never applied) or fewer than the literal-array length the migration declares. This converts the biggest blind spot from 'silent green' to 'checked'. Enumerate the expected functions + minimum counts from the migrations and keep them in a small reviewed table alongside the allowlist.

Replace the 400-char magic window with a robust anchor or widen it substantially (e.g. 2000) AND add a count-parity tripwire: raw-count every 'create ... trigger' keyword hit (minus known %-dynamic and comment sites) and FAIL CLOSED if the number of successfully extracted (name+ON) triggers is less than that raw count â€” this catches a single statement the regex silently failed to parse, which the current zero-total tripwire cannot.

Optionally return t.tgenabled in the prod query and FAIL (or warn-then-allowlist) when a declared trigger is present but tgenabled <> 'O', so a disabled security/audit trigger is not silently treated as satisfied.

Document that lexical filename sort must remain chronological and add a cheap assertion that every migration filename matches ^\d{14}_ (all 711 currently do) so a future non-timestamped filename cannot silently reorder last-op-wins.

prodSQL: select 'index' as kind, c.relname as identifier from pg_class c join pg_namespace n on n.oid = c.relnamespace where n.nspname = 'public' and c.relkind in ('i','I');
norm: Bare index relation name, double-quotes stripped, lowercased, with no schema prefix. Postgres index names are unique within a schema (indexes share the pg_class namespace), so the name alone is the full identity. CREATE INDEX never schema-qualifies the new name (the index inherits the target table's schema), and DROP INDEX's optional 'public.' prefix is stripped during extraction. Prod pg_class.relname for unquoted DDL is already folded to lowercase; the JS side lowercases both sides to be safe. Comparison is exact string equality of the normalized name.
fpFilters: public
if
not
exists
unique
concurrently
index
on
using
%I (never captured â€” begins with '%', outside [A-Za-z_]; the whole dynamic format('CREATE INDEX ... %I ...') statement yields no name and is a knownGap, not a false positive)

names occurring only inside stripped -- or /* */ comments (e.g. the 'CREATE INDEX takes a brief write lock' NOTE and the 'partial unique index on (message_id)' comment) are removed by comment-stripping before extraction
fixes: Make the dynamic-index companion assertion REQUIRED: enumerate the reference-table array x suffix set ({_search_idx,_name_trgm_idx,_data_idx,_category_idx,_placeholder,_description_source}) into the declared set (using the POST-rename table name reference_job_functions, not reference_team_functions) so those ~50-80 indexes are actually verified against prod, not just documented as a gap.

Fix the create/drop ordering to honor true statement order (scan CREATE and DROP in a single pass in match order, or split each file on ';' and apply per-statement) so within-file drop-then-recreate (idx_fleety_response_cache_embedding in 20260807130000) correctly ends up PRESENT and verified â€” making the spec's stated 'dropped then re-created ends up present' actually true.

Correct knownGap #4: ALTER INDEX ... RENAME TO statements DO exist (20260503180621 renames 6 reference_team_functions_* indexes to reference_job_functions_*). They strand no statically-declared name today (the old names are constraint/dynamic indexes), but the spec's 'None exist' claim is false, and once the dynamic indexes are allowlisted the allowlist MUST reference the new reference_job_functions_* names, since reference_team_functions_{search,name_trgm,data,category}_idx were renamed away.

Remove idx_email_send_log_message_sent_unique from sampleDeclared (it is dropped/replaced in 20260603205609); optionally add a positive test asserting a created-then-dropped-in-a-later-file index is EXCLUDED, and a test asserting a dropped-then-recreated-in-the-same-file index is INCLUDED (currently failing).
Add a knownGap/allowlist note for the framework MV _pk indexes that may be retired by the 20260817150000 facade repoint, to pre-empt a spurious MISSING failure at first CI run.

prodSQL:
-- Read-only. Returns one row per live RLS policy across ALL schemas (must NOT be restricted to public: storage.objects and realtime.messages carry declared policies). identifier is built to match extraction EXACTLY: lower(schema).lower(table) :: <exact policyname>. pg_policies is a pg_catalog view (schemaname, tablename, policyname, permissive, roles, cmd, qual, with_check).
SELECT 'policy' AS kind,
       lower(schemaname) || '.' || lower(tablename) || ' :: ' || policyname AS identifier
FROM pg_policies
ORDER BY identifier;
-- Note: no schema WHERE-clause on purpose. Extra Supabase-internal policies returned here are harmless (the gate only checks declared MINUS prod); omitting a declared schema, by contrast, would false-flag its policies. If payload size ever matters, the minimal safe filter is: WHERE schemaname IN ('public','storage','realtime') AND every schema the extractor emits is in that list â€” but unfiltered is the fail-safe choice.
norm: Identifier = `<schema>.<table> :: <policyName>` (separator is space-colon-colon-space, ` :: `). schema and table are lowercased on BOTH sides (extraction lowercases the captured schema/table; prod uses lower(schemaname)/lower(tablename)); schema defaults to `public` when the migration omits it (never omitted in this repo â€” 0 unqualified). policyName preserves EXACT case and spaces: for a double-quoted name, strip the surrounding quotes and unescape `""`->`"`; for a bare (unquoted) name, lowercase it (Postgres folds unquoted identifiers to lowercase, and pg_policies.policyname stores the folded form). Comparison is exact string equality of the full concatenated identifier. Examples that must match prod: `public.profiles :: Users can view their own profile`, `storage.objects :: Users can upload own avatar`, `realtime.messages :: Scoped realtime read access`, `public.reference_relationships :: fw_rel_read_active`.
fpFilters: Any match whose policy-name or table contains '%' (printf placeholders %I/%s/%L from EXECUTE format(...) loops) â€” these are runtime-generated, not concrete identifiers; exclude from the diff and route to the 'unresolved dynamic' fail-closed bucket (9 such CREATE statements in 20260502180318, 20260502184658, 20260502192050, 20260502193704). Never blanket-allowlist the literal '%I' string â€” that would hide drift.
Commented-out statements: strip /* */ and -- comments before matching so a disabled CREATE POLICY is not counted.
Do NOT treat schema literals 'storage' or 'realtime' as noise â€” they are REAL and must be fetched from prod (storage.objects=39, realtime.messages=7). Only 'public' is the default.

pg_policies self-references inside idempotency guards (SELECT ... FROM pg_policies WHERE policyname='X') are NOT matched (regex anchors on 'create/drop policy'), so no filter needed â€” noted only to preempt confusion.

Prose/Gherkin/seed-string phantoms (e.g. a fake table): none exist in this repo (loose 'create policy'==strict name+ON==484, all 188 tables real), but the regex structurally guards against them by requiring a well-formed `<name> ON [schema.]table` immediately after CREATE POLICY.
fixes: Harden identifierNormalization: explicitly strip surrounding double-quotes (and unescape ""->") from the SCHEMA and TABLE captures BEFORE lowercasing, exactly as done for the policy name. Currently only the name has documented quote handling; the table/schema regex groups include literal quotes. Prevents both a false-negative and a case-fold false-PASS on any future quoted-identifier policy. (My Norm() reference implementation that strips quotes reproduced all 458 keys correctly.)

Add a companion RLS/definition check for the 9 dynamic policies (assert each reference_* table has rowsecurity=true and the expected policy COUNT via pg_policies GROUP BY), and keep the unresolved-dynamic bucket fail-closed until each is allowlisted-with-reason. This closes the only real coverage hole.
Seed the drop-allowlist from the actual DROP-replay finally-dropped set (151 keys today), not the '~144' estimate; regenerate it from replay rather than hard-coding a number.

Optionally extend prod SQL to also return pg_policies.permissive/roles/cmd (and join pg_class.relrowsecurity) so a future phase can detect definition/RLS drift; today's name-only match is fine but document that a present-but-stale policy passes.

Keep the prod SQL UNFILTERED (no schema WHERE) as specified â€” verified correct: policies live only in public/storage/realtime today but an unfiltered query can never omit a declared schema; filtering is the only way to introduce a prod-side false pass.

prodSQL:
SELECT 'extension'::text AS kind,
       lower(e.extname)   AS identifier
FROM pg_catalog.pg_extension e
ORDER BY 2;
-- Returns every extension installed in the target database, name-only and lowercased,
-- to exactly match extraction normalization. NOT filtered by schema: extensions are
-- database-global and several here live outside public (pg_net/pgcrypto -> extensions,
-- pg_cron -> pg_catalog/cron, vector/pg_trgm relocated via ALTER EXTENSION SET SCHEMA).
-- Filtering by nspname would produce false GATE FAILURES for correctly-installed extensions.
norm: Extension NAME only (no schema), unquoted, lowercased, trimmed. E.g. `CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS pg_net SCHEMA extensions;` -> "pg_net"; `CREATE EXTENSION "uuid-ossp";` -> "uuid-ossp". Prod side: lower(pg_extension.extname). Schema/WITH SCHEMA/VERSION clauses are deliberately excluded from identity.
fpFilters: SQL line comments `-- ...` containing CREATE EXTENSION â€” REAL case: 20260707200000_recreate_cron_jobs_on_live_project.sql:32 `--   CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS pg_cron WITH SCHEMA cron;`. Neutralized by stripping `--` line comments and `/* */` block comments before matching (comment-aware, without deleting dollar-quoted bodies).
IF / NOT / EXISTS keywords are never captured as an extension name because the optional `(?:IF\s+NOT\s+EXISTS\s+)?` prefix is consumed first.

Dollar-quoted PROSE/Gherkin mentioning 'create extension' would over-extract a spurious name â€” NONE found for this category (all dollar-body CREATE EXTENSION hits, e.g. email_infra.sql:9 pg_cron, are genuine). If one ever appears, allowlist by name since it will not be a real Postgres extension. NOTE: do NOT filter out dollar-quoted CREATE EXTENSION wholesale â€” email_infra.sql:9 is a real declaration inside a DO block.

Supabase-preinstalled extensions returned by introspection but never declared in migrations (e.g. plpgsql, pg_stat_statements, uuid-ossp, pgjwt) are EXTRA live objects; the gate compares declared âŠ† live and must not fail on them.
fixes: Keep name-only identity for PRESENCE, but add a SECOND, non-fatal (or configurable-fatal) schema assertion to close the real blind spot: extend the prod SQL to also return the install schema â€” SELECT lower(e.extname) AS identifier, n.nspname AS schema FROM pg_catalog.pg_extension e JOIN pg_catalog.pg_namespace n ON n.oid = e.extnamespace â€” and, for any declared name whose final declared schema is resolvable (last WITH SCHEMA / SCHEMA clause, or an ALTER EXTENSION ... SET SCHEMA superseding it), assert it matches. This catches the extensions.gen_random_bytes-style breakage that presence-only misses.

Enable the optional ALTER EXTENSION regex (/\bALTER\s+EXTENSION\s+(?:"([^"]+)"|([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_$]*))/gi) and union its names into the declared set, so an ALTER-only reference to a never-CREATEd extension is still asserted present. Zero cost today (both ALTER'd names are already CREATEd) and removes the structural CREATE-only gap.

Make the dollar-quote-aware comment stripper an explicit, tested requirement (unit-test: a -- inside a $$...$$ body preceding a CREATE EXTENSION must NOT drop that declaration; a top-level -- CREATE EXTENSION must be dropped). This converts the currently-latent stripper invariant into an enforced one so a future migration can't induce a false negative.

Harden fail-closed beyond 'zero rows / timeout': also FAIL if the HTTP status is not 200, if the response body is not the expected JSON array shape, or if any row lacks the identifier field â€” so a malformed/partial prod response cannot be misread as 'all declared names present'.

Assert both comparison sides are lowercased at compare time (belt-and-suspenders): compare declared.map(toLowerCase) against live identifiers, so a future non-lowercase capture path (e.g. a quoted mixed-case name) cannot desync from lower(extname).

prodSQL:
SELECT
  'function'::text AS kind,
  n.nspname || '.' || p.proname || '(' || pg_get_function_identity_arguments(p.oid) || ')' AS identifier
FROM pg_catalog.pg_proc p
JOIN pg_catalog.pg_namespace n ON n.oid = p.pronamespace
WHERE n.nspname = 'public'
  AND p.prokind IN ('f','w')   -- plain + window functions created via CREATE FUNCTION; excludes aggregates 'a' and procedures 'p' (separate categories)
ORDER BY 2;
-- Read-only. pg_get_function_identity_arguments returns exactly the INPUT-arg types (no names, no DEFAULTs, no OUT args, no typmod) in Postgres-canonical spelling, e.g. '', 'text', 'uuid, text', 'text[]', 'vector', 'uuid, app_role' â€” the same identity used for DROP/overload resolution. The gate MUST pass this identifier's arg portion through the identical normalizeSignature() used on the migration side before set comparison, so alias/spelling differences collapse on both sides.
norm:
Identity string = "<schema>.<name>(<comma-joined normalized input-arg types>)", lowercased.
NAME: lowercase; strip surrounding double-quotes; if unqualified, prefix 'public.'. (No quoted/mixed-case/non-public names exist today, so lowercasing is safe.)
SIGNATURE (normalizeSignature): split the arg-list body on TOP-LEVEL commas (depth-aware over () and [] , skipping single-quoted literals) so commas inside numeric(10,2)/array/expr do not split. For each item:
  - CREATE side: drop trailing DEFAULT/`= expr`; drop a leading arg-mode keyword (exclude OUT-only items entirely; keep IN/INOUT/VARIADIC); the FIRST whitespace token is the arg name -> the TYPE is everything after it.
  - DROP side & prod side (pg_get_function_identity_arguments items): the WHOLE item is the type (type-only, no names).
  - normalizeType(type): lowercase; collapse whitespace; peel off & remember array suffix(es) matching /\[\s*\d*\s*\]$/ -> re-append as '[]' per level; strip trailing typmod '(...)' (Postgres stores no typmod on function args, so vector(768)->vector, numeric(10,2)->numeric, character varying(255)->character varying); strip a leading 'public.' on the type (custom types like app_role may print schema-qualified or bare depending on search_path); apply alias map: int|int4->integer, int2->smallint, int8|bigint->bigint, serial->integer(n/a to args), bool->boolean, varchar->character varying, char|bpchar->character, timestamptz->timestamp with time zone, timestamp->timestamp without time zone, timetz->time with time zone, time->time without time zone, decimal->numeric, float4->real, float8->double precision.
  Join normalized types with ', '. Zero-arg -> '' so identity ends with '()'.
Both the migration-extracted signature AND the prod pg_get_function_identity_arguments string are run through this SAME normalizeSignature(), guaranteeing convergence (the normalizer is idempotent on Postgres-canonical output). Comparison is exact string equality of the full identity string.
fpFilters: Comments: '-- Create function to generate ...' (yields phantom name 'to') and '-- ... on every CREATE FUNCTION (Supabase advisor ...' â€” removed by line-comment stripping; also excluded because the CREATE regex requires a real identifier immediately followed by '(' (the advisor line has 'FUNCTION (' with no identifier between).

Dollar-quoted body prose/Gherkin containing DDL-like text (e.g. 'CREATE TABLE public', 'public' as a fake object, EXECUTE-style strings) â€” removed by dollar-body stripping before matching; none of the 711 files actually build a function via EXECUTE 'CREATE FUNCTION ...'.
Schema literal 'public' must never be emitted as a standalone object name (it is the schema, not a function).

Placeholder/diagnostic DROPs that reference never-created names (public.your_audit_function_name(), public._diag_list_vault_names()) â€” harmless: removing an absent key from the identity set is a no-op.
prokind filter excludes aggregates ('a') and procedures ('p') so a same-named aggregate/procedure in prod is not mistaken for the declared function.
fixes: Canonicalize extension-schema types on BOTH sides. In normalizeType, after stripping typmod, strip a leading `extensions.` in addition to `public.` (or, more generally, strip any leading `<known-extension-schema>.` prefix: extensions, but keep the list explicit to avoid collapsing legitimately distinct schema-qualified types). This makes bare `vector` and `extensions.vector` converge. Given every custom/extension type name is unique across schemas in this corpus, stripping any single leading schema qualifier from type tokens is safe and is the most robust fix.

Make the prod type rendering deterministic: send `SET search_path = public, extensions;` before the SELECT in the same Management-API request (multi-statement), OR wrap the identifier so extension types render predictably. Combined with the strip-prefix normalization this removes the environment-dependence entirely.

Replace the dollar-body REGEX with a real tokenizing scanner that tracks open/close dollar tags and FAILS CLOSED (non-zero exit) on any unterminated or unbalanced tag, instead of silently over-consuming. This closes the silent-drop false negative. Do the same balanced scan for block/line comments so a dollar-quote-like sequence inside a comment cannot mis-pair.

Change name-only DROP handling to remove exactly one overload only when exactly one matching identity exists in the current declared set; if 2+ exist, treat it as a modeling error and fail closed (Postgres itself errors on ambiguous name-only DROP), rather than silently deleting all overloads and under-requiring.

Add a per-run assertion that the number of declared function identities is within an expected band (declaredCountApprox ~409) and fail closed if it drops sharply between runs -- a large unexplained drop is the fingerprint of dollar-strip over-consumption or a regex regression, complementing the existing zero-scan tripwire.

Add a self-test fixture exercising: an OUT-param function (identity must equal input args only, e.g. class_item_release -> (uuid, uuid)), a bare-`vector` vs `extensions.vector` overload, a name-only DROP, a DEFAULT containing a string with parens/commas, and a text[] arg -- so the normalizer's convergence and the parser's OUT/DEFAULT handling are proven, not assumed.
